messages:
tara: FYI CI is flaking when two containers run `redwoodctl login --headless --profile ci` concurrently — one process pauses ~8-12s and then proceeds.

omar: Repro locally with a tiny repro:
```
redwoodctl login --headless --profile ci &
redwoodctl login --headless --profile ci &
wait
```
Second process hangs with no browser URL printed.

ben: Sample log from the hung run: `WARN auth: cache lock active, waiting` then `ERROR auth: token refresh canceled`. Looks like the CLI's mkdir/marker lock under ~/.redwoodctl races on overlayfs/NFS.

tara: Workaround that helped in our runners: pre-create a token in the docker entrypoint or serialize login. Example entrypoint snippet we use: 
```
#!/bin/sh
: ${REDWOODCTL_PROFILE:=ci}
redwoodctl token create --profile "$REDWOODCTL_PROFILE" || true
exec "$@"
```
This avoids parallel login races without changing tests.

omar: Draft PR posted to replace the marker lock with an advisory fcntl lock + exponential backoff and to add a `--skip-token-cache` flag for ephemeral CI: gh:redwood/cli#499 (draft). On linux overlayfs the stall went away in my matrix runs.

ben: Please also fix `REDWOODCTL_PROFILE` precedence so headless login honors the env var unless `--profile` is explicit, and add jitter/backoff to token refresh retries (I saw 3 immediate retries skewing metrics).

ci-bot: CI: gh:redwood/cli#499 unit tests passed on linux-amd64 :white_check_mark:.

tara: Good. Can someone add a short note in devex docs about: 1) profile precedence, 2) using `--skip-token-cache` for ephemeral runners, and 3) the entrypoint snippet. If anyone sees post-merge hangs, capture the raw logs and runner FS type and ping @omar with details.
